newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stantronic off on profit-taking, dull debut.
newsitem.headline: Stantronic off on profit-taking, dull debut.

text.p: Shares in electrical and refrigeration company, Stantronic Ltd, fell five percent in early trade on Tuesday, a day after its listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Dealers said the firm had had a lacklustre debut, trading well below its expected 125 cent predicted opening price, and dipping further as investors took quick profits.
"It was really a dull (listing). People who got stock in the private placing took profits and more of this is going on today," a dealer said.
By 0830 GMT Stantronic shares were off five cents to 95 cents in volume of 78,900 securities.
Stantronic on Monday reverse-listed into the General Technologies Ltd cash shell to take a place in the market's electronics and electrical sector.
However, Harold Katz, Stantronic's operations director told Reuters the firm was very happy with the listing.
"The sky's the limit. We have a very young and dynamic management team. The group is also very acquisition-wise. In the last 10 years we have done 10 acquisitions," he said.

"The creation of the Stantronic group as a listed company has generated the working capital required for the group to take advantage of future growth opportunities, including those for new acquisitions," the company said.
